description:
Aggregate the work that delivers this outcome: CLI and in-process tests use one definition of each fixture and never change process-wide state.

## Background

This story groups the test-topology tasks that share one design surface, so they can be reviewed together once each has landed.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One shared fixture spawns `jit` for every CLI test, and no test file defines its own binary locator, repository setup or id scraping from human-readable output.
- [hard] REQ-02: Issue construction, the taxonomy repository and the memory executor each have one definition in shared test support, and the memory executor is set up by product initialisation.
- [hard] REQ-03: Tests that need the shipped item kinds derive them from the shipped default package.
- [hard] REQ-04: Tests never change process-wide state (working directory, environment variables); a value a test varies is passed explicitly. Every test passes alone, in any order and in parallel.





## Evidence

REQ-04, at `0b4874edf` unless stated. `git grep` finds no `set_current_dir`, `env::set_var` or `env::remove_var` under `crates/`. Each test in its own process under nextest: serial 4632/4632, 32 threads 4632/4632, hash partitions 1-3 (1546, 1524, 1562) each with the rest absent. Tests sharing a process: 20 shuffled runs at `b5f2d9730`, seeds 1-20, all 14 test executables, 92,680 passed (87d5fd34).

This reaches order within a target, by libtest's unstable shuffle flag, and not order across targets, which never share a process. nextest has no shuffle, so its per-process isolation is what covers order there.
title: Tests run on shared fixtures
